raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Small fixes to the NPU MLA KV pool, found while serving GLM-5.2 with 1M-token contexts on Ascend A3.

1. **DCP on NPU: the allocator page and the index-K bound.** `_alloc_page_size` did not ask the NPU allocator,
   whose page is `page_size * dcp_size` (CUDA, HIP and XPU already do). This only changes behaviour at
   `--page-size 1`, which DSA on Ascend cannot run today (the Lightning Indexer needs a block size that is a
   multiple of 16), so it is a latent bug. Index-K writes also had no bounds check against the widened index range.
2. **A pool that cannot hold one full-length request fails late.** When the pool is smaller than
   `--context-length`, nothing is logged at startup. Long requests are refused or truncated at serving time.

This PR first also removed the `is_arch35` gate on the compact index-K layout. #44436 has since made the same
change on main, so that part is gone from this diff. Only a test that both sides agree is left (see Tests).

## Modifications

- `allocation.py`: `_alloc_page_size` returns the NPU allocator's page size under DCP, as on CUDA/HIP/XPU.
- `memory_pool_npu.py`: `set_index_k_buffer` checks writes against the widened index range (async
  out-of-bounds check, active with `SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT=1`).
- `TpModelWorker.get_worker_info`: a startup warning when the served `kv_capacity` is below `--context-length`.
  It is checked there because that is the final served value, so DCP and page-interleave widening are counted.
- `kv_cache_configurator.py`, `pool_configurator.py`: comments on why the NPU DCP allocator is widened and why
  the indexer term scales with `dcp_size`.

**Behaviour change for users without DCP:** none, except the new warning when the pool is short.

## Accuracy Tests

No forward-path change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed change.

## Tests

- `test/registered/unit/managers/test_dcp_logical_capacity.py` (CPU), new case
  `test_short_pool_warning_uses_served_capacity`: dcp1 serves fewer tokens than the context and warns; dcp2
  widens the same rows past it and does not.
- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_npu_index_k_elision.py` (CPU): on A2/A3 the memory budget and the pool
  count the same Indexer layers. The tests #44436 added check each side on its own; this one fails if only one
  side changes.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

For hybrid  sliding-window attention with `--enable-unified-memory`, the warning uses `sizes.max_total_num_tokens`, which is a sizing estimate rather than the effective serving capacity.

`ModelRunner` uses `hybrid_swa_token_capacity()` based on `allocator.size_full`, optionally capped by `max_total_tokens`. This mismatch can produce a false warning.

For example, with an estimated capacity of 80K tokens, an effective capacity of 130K, and `context_len=100K`, the warning incorrectly reports insufficient KV memory.

**Suggested fix:** Use the initialized allocator's effective capacity, consistent with serving, while preserving DCP/KV-sharding scaling and draft-worker exclusion.

The comment disagrees with the expression one line below it. 
This comment says the OOB bound is "one widened page past index_size", but the formula right below it uses 'index_page_padding' pages, not 1.

Where does `index_page_padding` come from:
    662: global_page_padding = self.dcp_size if self.dcp_size > 1 else 1
    664: index_page_padding  = global_page_padding  (when there is an Indexer)

So when DCP is on, 'index_page_padding = attn_dcp_size' — 8 or 16 pages, not 1.

+"""On A3 the index-K budget and the pool must elide the same layers.
+
+[Test Category] Correctness
+[Test Target] mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py  (_build_ascend_mla_kv_pool)
+              model_executor/pool_configurator.py (_compute_dsa_indexer_cell_size)
+
+If only one side elides, the pool overruns its budget or wastes the elided rows.
+"""
+
+import types
+import unittest
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.kv_cache_configurator import KVCacheConfigurator
+from sglang.srt.model_executor import pool_configurator
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_context
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+INDEX_HEAD_DIM = 128
+# GLM-5.2-like: only some layers own an Indexer, the rest reuse top-k.
+INDEXER_TYPES = [
+    "full",
+    "shared",
+    "shared",
+    "full",
+    "shared",
+    "shared",
+    "full",
+    "shared",
+]
+NUM_LAYERS = len(INDEXER_TYPES)
+INDEXER_LAYERS = (0, 3, 6)
+
+
+def _kvc():
+    return types.SimpleNamespace(
+        model_config=types.SimpleNamespace(
+            hf_config=types.SimpleNamespace(
+                architectures=["GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM"],
+                index_topk=2048,
+                index_head_dim=INDEX_HEAD_DIM,
+                indexer_types=INDEXER_TYPES,
+            ),
+            kv_lora_rank=512,
+            qk_rope_head_dim=64,
+            index_head_dim=INDEX_HEAD_DIM,
+        ),
+        layer_info=types.SimpleNamespace(
+            start_layer=0, end_layer=NUM_LAYERS, num_effective_layers=NUM_LAYERS
+        ),
+        server_args=types.SimpleNamespace(enable_hisparse=False),
+        mambaish_config=None,
+        is_draft_worker=False,
+        kv_cache_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        device="cpu",
+    )
+
+
+class TestNpuIndexKElision(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        super().setUp()
+        override = get_context().override_server_args(page_size=128)
+        override.install()
+        self.addCleanup(override.restore)
+
+    @patch("sglang.srt.hardware_backend.npu.utils.is_npu_arch35", return_value=False)
+    @patch.object(pool_configurator, "_is_npu", True)
+    def test_a3_budget_and_pool_count_the_same_indexer_layers(self, _):
+        kvc = _kvc()
+        with patch(
+            "sglang.srt.hardware_backend.npu.memory_pool_npu.NPUMLATokenToKVPool"
+        ) as pool_cls:
+            KVCacheConfigurator._build_ascend_mla_kv_pool(
+                kvc, max_total_num_tokens=1024, is_dsa_model=True
+            )
+        self.assertEqual(pool_cls.call_args.kwargs["indexer_layer_ids"], INDEXER_LAYERS)
+
+        cell_size = (
+            pool_configurator.DefaultPoolConfigurator._compute_dsa_indexer_cell_size(
+                None, kvc=kvc, num_layers=NUM_LAYERS
+            )
+        )
+        bf16_bytes = 2
+        self.assertEqual(cell_size, INDEX_HEAD_DIM * len(INDEXER_LAYERS) * bf16_bytes)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

For hybrid  sliding-window attention with `--enable-unified-memory`, the warning uses `sizes.max_total_num_tokens`, which is a sizing estimate rather than the effective serving capacity.

`ModelRunner` uses `hybrid_swa_token_capacity()` based on `allocator.size_full`, optionally capped by `max_total_tokens`. This mismatch can produce a false warning.

For example, with an estimated capacity of 80K tokens, an effective capacity of 130K, and `context_len=100K`, the warning incorrectly reports insufficient KV memory.

**Suggested fix:** Use the initialized allocator's effective capacity, consistent with serving, while preserving DCP/KV-sharding scaling and draft-worker exclusion.

The comment disagrees with the expression one line below it. 
This comment says the OOB bound is "one widened page past index_size", but the formula right below it uses 'index_page_padding' pages, not 1.

Where does `index_page_padding` come from:
    662: global_page_padding = self.dcp_size if self.dcp_size > 1 else 1
    664: index_page_padding  = global_page_padding  (when there is an Indexer)

So when DCP is on, 'index_page_padding = attn_dcp_size' — 8 or 16 pages, not 1.

inline_comments.body: This PR only removes the `is_arch35` gate, so A3 now runs the compact-layout code A5 already runs on main. The new A3 risk is the pool and the memory budget eliding different layers, which `test_npu_index_k_elision.py` covers. An end-to-end test needs GLM-5.2 on 16–32 A3 dies for about an hour per run, which is why the existing GLM-5.2 test is nightly-only and disabled. A unit read-back test would add little: reads and writes share one layer-to-slot lookup, and a wrong slot crashes on the first forward. We validated on an A3 box with GLM-5.2 instead: the pool grew 15.28% as predicted, and GSM8K stayed within noise.
